assessments.scope:
End User Computing has asked to replace the built-in Windows extraction feature with a dedicated archive utility that can open additional formats (7z, RAR, TAR, GZ) and create encrypted archives.

In scope: the desktop application and its right-click menu entries on corporate Windows laptops and virtual desktops, the installer and packaging process, the update mechanism, default settings, and how extracted files are handled by Windows and endpoint protection.

Out of scope: use on servers, the command-line version, macOS devices and OT workstations. Each needs its own review before the utility is installed there.

This is a sample assessment with illustrative answers. Replace the product details, people and results with your own before relying on it.
assessments.summaryComments:
The archive utility was reviewed as commercial desktop software for about 2,400 users. It runs entirely on the workstation under the signed-in user's account, has no server or cloud component, and has no AI capability. No NERC CIP impact is expected for the scope reviewed.

The solution risk level is High because the utility opens untrusted files from outside the company and extraction engines are a regular target for attackers. Six recommendations are listed below. With the packaged build, enforced settings, patching and endpoint rules in place, each risk comes down to Low or Very Low.

Cyber Risk does not object to the request provided the recommendations marked Mitigate are implemented before deployment. Any extension to servers, macOS or OT workstations requires a further review.
assessments.solutionOverview:
A desktop utility that opens, extracts and creates compressed archive files. It adds entries to the right-click menu in File Explorer and registers itself as the default program for common archive formats. Staff use it to open archives received from customers, suppliers and software vendors, and to package files for transfer.

Installation needs administrator rights and will be done only through the software centre. The utility itself runs with the signed-in user's rights.

It keeps no business data of its own: only settings and a list of recently opened archives in the user's profile, plus temporary copies when a file is opened directly from inside an archive. The only network traffic is an optional check for updates and optional usage telemetry, both of which can be switched off by policy.

It supports AES-256 encryption for new archives and, for compatibility, the older and weak ZIP encryption.
assessments.topRisks:
A crafted archive exploits a flaw in the extraction engine and runs code on the workstation. The vendor has fixed four such flaws in the last 24 months.
Extracted files lose their "downloaded from the internet" marking under default settings, so Windows warnings and Office protected view do not apply to them.
The installer or a later update is tampered with before it reaches workstations, or staff download a look-alike installer from an unofficial site.
Password-protected archives cannot be opened by the mail and web gateways, so their contents reach the workstation unscanned.
Staff use the weak ZIP encryption to send Confidential or Customer data outside the company.
A deliberately oversized archive fills the disk on a workstation or virtual desktop.

recommendations.recommendation: Add the utility to third-party patching with the standard windows, deploy out of cycle when a flaw is being actively exploited, and remove older versions during deployment.
recommendations.treatment: End User Computing will add the utility to the monthly third-party patching cycle before deployment. Due 1 December 2026. Compensating controls: endpoint protection on all workstations, and users have no administrator rights.

recommendations.recommendation: Turn on carrying the "downloaded from the internet" marking onto extracted files for all formats, and enforce the setting centrally so users cannot change it.
recommendations.treatment: The setting will be enforced by policy in the packaged build and tested before release. Due 24 November 2026.

recommendations.recommendation: Download the installer from the vendor's site only, check its signature and published hash at packaging, deploy only through the software centre, and disable the utility's own update check.
recommendations.treatment: Signature and hash checks are part of the standard packaging checklist. Update checks and telemetry will be disabled by policy. Due 24 November 2026.

recommendations.recommendation: Quarantine inbound password-protected archive attachments for review, and add an endpoint rule that blocks programs and scripts started directly from archive temporary folders.
recommendations.treatment: The endpoint rule is due 8 December 2026 and the mail gateway change 15 December 2026. Until then, endpoint protection scans files as they are extracted.

recommendations.recommendation: Hide or disable the weak ZIP encryption option so new encrypted archives use AES-256, and remind staff that the secure file transfer service is the approved route for external transfers.
recommendations.treatment: The weak option will be hidden by policy in the packaged build. Staff guidance will be published by 15 December 2026.

recommendations.recommendation: No further action for oversized archives. The utility warns before extracting when the expanded size exceeds free disk space, and virtual desktop profiles have storage quotas.
recommendations.treatment: Accepted by the business at the current level. The impact is limited to a single workstation and is quickly recovered.
